Implementing Artificial Intelligence in a Gastroenterology Practice
  • Source: Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Vol. 26, Issue (2026)
  • Topic: AI administrative platform implementation in gastroenterology practice
  • Author(s): Aisenberg J, Bamji N, Hertz D, Allen JI
1. Practice Profile
  • 24-physician independent GI practice in New York City
  • 8 clinical offices + 3 ambulatory endoscopy centers
  • Owns: pathology laboratory, infusion practice, clinical research division
  • Staff-to-provider ratio ~5:1
1.1 Pre-AI Operational Challenges
  • Patient on-hold times >4 minutes during peak hours
  • Call abandonment rate: 15%
  • After-hours calls (4 PM–9 AM) → generic answering service → appointment leakage
  • Multiple siloed technology platforms (not unified operating environment)
  • Staff navigating multiple systems with unstructured data and complex workflow rules
2. AI Implementation Partnership (2025)
  • Partnered with Next Dimension AI (startup focused on LLM-based healthcare administration)
  • Practice contributed: established workflows, operational knowledge, high volume/complexity, financial resources
  • AI partner contributed: AI expertise, voice technology, software engineering, systems integration
2.1 Development Approach
  • "Human-in-the-loop" model → engineers embedded alongside staff
  • Incremental deployment with validation on limited volumes before expansion
  • Committee of physicians + administrative leaders for review/approval
  • AI supports administrative functions only, not clinical decisions
  • No full-time employee terminations from AI implementation
3. Six AI Agents Deployed
3.1 Reception Agent
  • Identifies itself as AI
  • Determines reason for patient's call
  • Resolves simple questions or routes to appropriate agent/staff
3.2 Appointment Agent
  • Schedules office visits, telehealth, procedures
  • Coordinates patient requests with provider availability, payer requirements, provider-specific preferences
3.3 Medical Records Agent
  • Documents medical records requests
  • Captures delivery information → routes to appropriate staff
3.4 Prescription Agent
  • Documents refill requests
  • Confirms patient's preferred pharmacy → submits to provider for review/approval
3.5 Procedure Prior Authorization Agent
  • Reviews clinical information within EHR
  • Extracts supporting documentation
  • Interfaces with payer portals → files approvals in patient chart
3.6 Procedure Preparation Agent
  • Answers common pre-procedure preparation questions
4. Platform Features
  • Centralized AI platform with all agents intercommunicating
  • Integrated with EHR and other databases
  • Voice + text messaging available 24/7
  • All AI-patient interactions: recorded, transcribed, reviewable
  • Dashboard shows: agent activity, escalations, follow-up tasks, performance metrics
  • CRM functionality → tracks unresolved requests + manages follow-up
5. Implementation Timeline & Scaling
5.1 Initial Deployment (October 2025)
  • Reception Agent launched for after-hours calls without EHR integration
  • Demonstrated patients willing to interact with AI for routine administrative needs
5.2 Expansion Phase (January 2026)
  • Prescription Refill + Appointment Scheduling Agents → full EHR integration
  • Shifted AI from passive message-taking to active participant in clinical operations
5.3 Full Deployment Results (January–May 2026)
  • AI agents resolved 61.5% of calls without human interaction
  • 38.5% routed to staff
  • Of routed calls: 73.4% = patient preference for human (not technical limitation)
5.4 Call Volume Progression
Month Calls to AI % of Incoming Resolution Rate
Feb 2026 4,347/13,551 32% 92%
Mar 2026 9,539 66% 57%
Apr 2026 11,162 92% 60%
May 2026 10,043 76% 64.4%
6. Patient Access Improvements
  • On-hold time: 3 min 14 sec → 15 seconds (April 2026)
  • Peak hour on-hold: 6 min 3 sec → 34 seconds
  • Call abandonment rate: 10.2%–12.3% → 1.9%
  • AI eliminated traditional telephone queues for routine requests
  • All abandoned calls → AI alerted staff + staff contacted patient
6.1 Single-Day Scheduling Snapshot (April 14, 2026)
  • AI booked 91/152 newly scheduled appointments (60%)
  • 13 call center staff booked remaining 61 (40%)
7. Procedure Prior Authorization Results
  • May 2026: AI agent resolved 73% of procedural authorization requirements autonomously
  • Only 27% escalated to staff → substantially reduced administrative workload
8. Patient Acceptance & Satisfaction
  • Appointment Scheduling Agent: 87% satisfaction rate
  • Medical Records Agent: 82% satisfaction rate
  • Prescription Refill Agent: 79% satisfaction rate
  • Procedure Preparation Agent: 64% satisfaction rate
8.1 Continuous Improvement Process
  • Administrative staff + physicians routinely review patient complaints and recorded AI interactions
  • Review shows: AI often followed protocols appropriately → dissatisfaction stemmed from preference for human over technical failure
  • Training data used to iteratively improve: conversational responses, decision pathways, escalation criteria
9. Staff & Physician Acceptance
9.1 Physician Acceptance (High)
  • 5 physicians participated in AI oversight committee
  • Reported: improved message timeliness/accuracy, reduced after-hours bowel prep calls
  • AI helped fill appointment slots from night-before scheduling
9.2 Staff Adoption (Strong)
  • Administrative staffing reduced through attrition only
  • Re-purposed front office staff from routine tasks → nuanced clinical information calls
  • Staff reported: less rushed, improved job satisfaction, higher service level
9.3 Administrator Perspective
  • AI "de-risked" operations → less dependent on workforce availability
  • Less susceptible to: weather disruptions, absenteeism, hiring challenges, workforce instability
  • Reduced administrative cost per encounter → increased patient volume without proportional labor/overhead increase
10. Key Success Factors
  • Close collaboration between clinical + technical teams
  • Human-in-the-loop development model
  • Incremental deployment with continuous performance monitoring
  • Seamless integration with existing clinical workflows + EHR systems
  • Standardized approach → deployment in additional practices within 60–90 days
11. Future Implications
  • AI administrative agents → important opportunity to:
  • ↓ administrative burden
  • ↑ patient access
  • ↑ practice efficiency
  • AI assumes routine administrative work → physicians/staff more time for:
  • Complex clinical decision-making
  • Communication + empathy (uniquely human)
  • Future of AI in healthcare determined by:
  • Increasingly capable foundation models
  • Organizations' ability to redesign workflows, establish governance, integrate AI safely
